TRREB.kpis: July reads as a balanced market across TRREB, with the sales to new listings ratio now up 6 months in a row and months of inventory down 3 months in a row. The single most useful message for your clients is that the region has tightened steadily while staying balanced. That gives you room to set realistic expectations on both sides of a deal.
TRREB.price: The average price sits at $1,003,956, down 5.2% from last month and 4.5% from a year ago. The median came in at $860,000, off 5.5% year over year. Tell your sellers pricing has softened on both measures, and show your buyers that entry points are more forgiving than they were last summer.
TRREB.balance: With 4.6 months of inventory and a sales to new listings ratio of 37.1%, up 0.6 points, neither side holds a decisive edge. Properties are closing at 97% of list. Use that spread to keep sellers grounded on asking prices and to show buyers where reasonable offers land.
TRREB.activity: Sales reached 5,995, down 0.9% year over year, while new listings fell 17.8% to 14,484 and active listings dropped 12.1% to 26,098. Homes are taking 45 days to sell. With supply pulling back faster than demand, coach buyers to move deliberately rather than wait for a flood of choice.

Halton.kpis: Halton holds in balanced territory, with the sales to new listings ratio up 6 months in a row and months of inventory down 4 months in a row. The clearest point for your clients is that this region has been firming up quietly for half a year. Frame it as steady rather than sudden.
Halton.price: The average price of $1,151,595 is down 5.8% month over month but still up 0.2% year over year, one of the few positive annual reads in the GTA. The median tells a softer story at $970,000, down 7.6% from last year. Walk your clients through both figures so nobody anchors to a single number.
Halton.balance: At 4.2 months of inventory and a sales to new listings ratio of 39.5%, up 0.4 points, the negotiating table is even. Deals are landing at 96% of list price. That gap gives buyers a defensible starting point and reminds sellers that overreaching on price extends the wait.
Halton.activity: Sales of 682 slipped 4.1% year over year, while new listings dropped 16.9% to 1,503 and active listings fell 15.3% to 2,659. At 52 days on market, patience is required on both sides. With inventory thinning, position well priced listings to stand out rather than assume time alone will produce an offer.

Peel.kpis: Peel is a balanced market where sales are actually rising against a shrinking supply. The sales to new listings ratio has climbed 6 months in a row and months of inventory has eased 3 months in a row. Tell your clients demand is holding while listings pull back, which is the tension worth watching here.
Peel.price: The average price is $910,007, down 5.8% from last month and 6.4% from a year ago. The median of $851,000 is off 5.4% year over year. Both readings point the same way, so give your sellers a candid picture and show your buyers the improvement in affordability versus last July.
Peel.balance: With 5.0 months of inventory and a sales to new listings ratio of 34.0%, up 0.7 points, leverage is shared. Sales are completing at 97% of list. Use that ratio to keep sellers realistic and to help buyers calibrate offers that get taken seriously.
Peel.activity: Sales rose 1.6% to 1,053 even as new listings fell 18.7% to 2,875 and active listings dropped 13.2% to 5,055. Homes are averaging 48 days to sell. With fewer listings competing, advise sellers to price accurately from day one and remind buyers that choice is narrowing.

Toronto.kpis: Toronto sits in balanced territory with sales edging higher against tighter supply. The sales to new listings ratio is up 6 months in a row and months of inventory is down 4 months in a row. The most useful line for your clients is that the city is absorbing inventory faster while staying balanced overall.
Toronto.price: The average price of $1,010,836 fell 6.5% month over month and 3.3% year over year, the steepest monthly move among the regions. The median of $800,000 is down 5.9% from a year ago. Prepare sellers for a more competitive pricing environment and let buyers know the numbers have come toward them.
Toronto.balance: At 4.6 months of inventory and a sales to new listings ratio of 38.1%, up 0.7 points, neither party dictates terms. Closings are running at 97% of list. That consistency gives you a firm reference point when framing offers and counteroffers.
Toronto.activity: Sales climbed 2.4% to 2,242 while new listings dropped 17.2% to 4,980 and active listings fell 13.5% to 9,310. At 37 days on market, Toronto is the quickest mover in the GTA. Use that pace to press buyers on decisiveness and to justify sharp, accurate list prices for sellers.
